chunks: Abdullah ibn Kaysan informed me, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).
He said: I said to him, 'May I be made your ransom, I am your devotee Abdullah ibn Kaysan.' He said: 'As for the lineage, I recognise it; but as for you, I do not recognise you.'

He said: I said to him, 'I was born in the mountains and grew up in the land of Persia. I mix with people in business and other matters. I come across a man and see in him good conduct, good morals, and abundant trustworthiness — then I investigate and find him to be an enemy of yours. And I come across a man and see from him evil morals, little trustworthiness, and malice — then I investigate and find him to be one of your followers. How can this be?'

Then he said to me: 'Did you not know, O son of Kaysan, that God, Mighty and Majestic, took a clay from Paradise and a clay from the Fire, then mixed them both together, then separated this from that and that from this? So what you saw in those ones — the trustworthiness, good morals, and good conduct — is from what the clay of Paradise touched them with, and they will return to what they were created from. And what you saw in these ones — the little trustworthiness, evil morals, and malice — is from what the clay of the Fire touched them with, and they will return to what they were created from.'

key_terms.السمت: Conduct/demeanor — outward appearance, bearing, and manner of behavior in public
key_terms.العداوة: Enmity — opposition to and rejection of the authority of the Imams
key_terms.الولاية: Wilayah — allegiance and devotion to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.زعارّة: Malice/meanness — a rare Quranic/classical word for moral baseness, corruption, or aggressiveness
key_terms.طينة: Clay/essence — in Shia cosmology, the primordial substance from which each person's soul-essence was created, determining their spiritual orientation

ai.seo_question: Why do some enemies of the Imams have good morals while some followers have bad morals in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In this narration, a companion named Abdullah ibn Kaysan presents a puzzling observation to Imam al-Sadiq (AS): enemies of the Imams sometimes display exemplary character, while followers sometimes exhibit moral failings. The Imam resolves the paradox through a cosmological doctrine: God took clay from both Paradise and the Fire, mixed them, then separated them. Every human being carries a trace of both clays, and the dominant clay determines their eventual destiny — believers bear the imprint of paradise clay and will return to it, disbelievers bear the imprint of fire clay and will return to it. This doctrine, known in Shia theology as the doctrine of 'tina' (clay/essence), explains why external morality does not alone determine a person's inner nature or eschatological fate.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and someone else, from Al Husayn Bin Al Hassan, altogether from Muhammad Bin Awrama, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Ismail Bin Yasaar, from Usman Bin Yusuf who said, ‘Abdullah Bin Kaysan infromed me,

(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, said, ‘I said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘I am your<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> friend Abdullah Bin Kaysan’. He<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said: ‘As for the lineage, so I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> recognise it, and as for you, so I<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> do not recognise you’.

I said to him<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup>, ‘I was born in the mountains and grew up in the land of Persia, and I tend to blend in with the people regarding business and other than that. So I came across the man and I saw him as a good listener and good manners and a lot of trustworthiness. When I investigate I find him to be one of your<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> enemies; and I came across the man and saw evil manners from him, and as being of little trustworthiness, and meanness. When I investigate I find him to be one of your<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> friends. So how did that happen?’

So he<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> said to me: ‘But, do you not know, O Ibn Kaysan, that Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Took a clay from the Paradise and a clay from the Fire. So He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Blended the two together. Then He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> Removed this from this, and this from this. Thus, what you see from those as being the ones of trustworthiness, and goodly mannerisms, and as good listeners, so it is from what has touched them from the clay of the Paradise, and they would be returning to what they had been Created from; and what you see from these as being of the ones with little trustworthiness, and evil mannerisms, and the meanness, so it is from what touched them from the clay of the Fire, and they would be returning to what they had been Created from’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad, who has narrated from more than one person from al-Husayn ibn al-Hassan. All of the above have narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Uwarma from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Isma’il ibn Yasar from ‘Uthman ibn Yusuf who has said that, reported to him ‘Abd Allah ibn Kaysan, from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.)

who has said the following: “Once I said to the Imam, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, I am your servant, abu ‘Abd Allah ibn Kaysan.’ The Imam said, ‘I know your genealogy. However, I do not know you (so well).’

I said, ‘I was born in the mountains and grew up in the land of Persia. I associate with people in business and other occasions. I, thus, associate with a man and find his appearance very good, to be of good manners and more trustworthy. When I investigate 1 find him to be one of your enemies. I also associate with another man who has bad manners, is less trustworthy and hot tempered. I then investigate and find him to be of your supporters and followers. Why is it so?’

“He (the Imam) said, ‘O ibn Kaysan, Allah, the Majestic, the Glorious, took a clay from paradise and also from fire and then mixed them together. Then He separated this from that and that from this. The good appearances, good manners and trustworthiness that you find in them (our enemies) is because of the touch of the clay from paradise but they will return to that from which they are made. The deceitfulness, bad manners and hot-temperament that you find in them (our supporters and followers) is because of the touch of the clay from fire, however, they will return to that from which they were made.’”
